html:
The Homalco, Xwémalhkwu in their own language, are a Northern Coast Salish people of Bute Inlet, a long fjord on the mainland coast of British Columbia, north of the Strait of Georgia.

With the Klahoose and the Tla'amin they were known as the Mainland Comox, and they speak the same language. They fished the salmon runs of the Homathko and Southgate rivers. In 1864 a road crew building a route from Bute Inlet to the gold fields was killed by Tsilhqot'in warriors, starting the Chilcotin War. Many Homalco later moved to villages on Vancouver Island and the outer islands.
